Locked with a non-mutation unit test in `tests/unit/translator-gemini-consecutive-role-2191.test.ts`.

Fixed in commit 69f0735c.

`applyAppendSystemBlock` now:
- When `idempotencyKey` is set: scans **all** blocks for a prefix match.
- When not set: falls back to exact-text match across **all** blocks (not just the last).
- This prevents duplicate appends even when blocks are interleaved.

Applied the regex change as suggested — replaced `normalizedModel.includes("deepseek")` with `/(^|\/)deepseek/i.test(normalizedModel)`. This narrows the match to segment boundaries while remaining compatible with the `deepseek-ai/` prefix format used in the registry.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Confirmed and fixed in 403a82be. The bare-slug path goes through `MODEL_MAP[model] ?? model`, so when a caller passes `gpt-5-4-t-mini` directly both `modelId` and `slug` end up as that string, neither contains `thinking`, and the substring check returned false.

Generalized the fix instead of hardcoding the one slug: derived `THINKING_CAPABLE_SLUGS` from `MODEL_MAP` (any value whose key contains `thinking` or is `o3`), so future thinking-mini abbreviations auto-extend the check. Added a parameterised regression covering `gpt-5-4-t-mini`, `gpt-5-5-thinking`, and `o3` as bare-slug inputs.

@gemini-code-assist[bot] addressed in the latest push. I moved `normalizeCliCompatProviderId` into a shared helper (`src/shared/utils/cliCompat.ts`) and now both the UI constants and `open-sse/config/cliFingerprints.ts` import the same implementation, so the Copilot -> GitHub normalization has a single source of truth. Re-ran the focused fingerprint tests plus core/noimplicit typechecks successfully.
providerSpecificData is always a flat `Record<string, unknown>` by convention (never nested) — shallow merge is safe and intentional here.
